ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporation Law); Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT Omnibus Law), as amended by Ley No. 70 de 23 de octubre de 2019; applicable implementing regulations issued by the General Directorate of Revenue and the Registro Público regarding beneficial ownership filings.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social / Acta de Constitución)
Certificate of Legal Existence and Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registry in the Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney and Certified Passport Copy of Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary / Passport Authority in Country of Origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN/SSI lists, United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, EU and UK sanctions lists, and Panama’s domestic financial and terrorist designation lists; PEP screening (including foreign PEPs) requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring in accordance with the risk-based approach under Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Servicios en Línea / Portal de Trámites en Línea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in Spanish or any language using Latin script; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters for registry indexing and publication. All registered name documentation shall be submitted in Spanish and must avoid duplicative or misleading similarity with existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected or challenged, the applicant or its registered agent may file a reconsideration request with the Director General of the Registro Público within five (5) business days of the rejection notice, stating factual grounds and proposing a corrected name. In the event of a reaffirmed rejection, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal under the general administrative procedure (Ley 38 de 2000), and thereafter before the competent administrative court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Sociedad Anónima must maintain a physical registered office at the licensed resident agent’s address in Panama. A virtual or co-working office may be used as an ancillary administrative address for business correspondence, client meetings, and logistics back-office support, but it may not substitute for the statutory registered office required for public register, tax, and legal service of process purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this non-licensed light logistics / 3PL kitting scope; quantified annual unannounced on-site inspection probability is approximately 0.8/10 for the first year. Inspections remain discretionary where PEP relationships, adverse media, or fiscal irregularities are identified by the tax administration or AML/CFT supervisors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (Panama Companies Act for Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Ley 5 de 2011 (authorized capital in freely convertible currency, shares without par value) and Ley 70 de 2017 (mandatory registered agent, abolition of bearer shares). Key provisions: Art. 2 (method of incorporation by public deed), Art. 5 (content of the articles of incorporation), Art. 7 (legal personality acquired upon inscription in the Public Registry), Arts. 13-31 (capital stock and share ledger), Arts. 38-48 (directors and first board governance).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Mercantil (Mercantile Registry Section), Folio Electrónico Division, Avenida Justo Arosemena, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública Constitutiva (Public Deed of Incorporation) submitted for mandatory inscription as a Sociedad Anónima in the Mercantile Folio (Folio Electrónico).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required by Panamanian law. The articles of incorporation commonly declare authorized capital of at least USD 10,000 divided into registered (nominative) common shares; such capital may be fully or partially unpaid, and subscribed shares must be entered in the Share Register. Bearer shares are prohibited under Ley 70 de 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [PA_CORP], a Panama Sociedad Anónima. WHEREAS, the incorporators have subscribed the authorized capital as stated in the Public Deed of Incorporation; and WHEREAS, the Company requires a registered office, a statutory agent, and officers to conduct lawful business, IT IS RESOLVED: 1. The share subscription is ratified and entered in the Share Register. 2. The registered office is established at [Registered Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the statutory agent is appointed. 3. The following officers are elected: President, Secretary, and Treasurer. 4. The said officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file all required registrations. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Mercantile Portal (Registro Público en Línea) or in-person at the Mercantile Information Window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance application (Certificado de Averiguación de Nombre) providing three proposed corporate names in order of preference. The Registrar verifies that the chosen name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company. Once approved, the name is reserved for 30 calendar days, within which the incorporation deed must be filed or the reservation lapses.
required_dossiers: List of three proposed corporate names
Identity documents of incorporators or instructing attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused as confusingly similar, the instructing attorney may refile with alternate names. A clerical rejection may be cured by filing a written reconsideration request (escrito de reconsideración) with the Registrar without loss of the application fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Escritura Pública (Public Deed of Incorporation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública / Notary Public of the First Judicial District, Panama City (licensed Panamanian attorney).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators, either personally or through an apostilled power of attorney granted to the attorney-in-fact, appear before the notary to execute the public deed. The deed must contain: the reserved corporate name, corporate purpose (ISIC 5210 / NAICS 493110 fulfillment, kitting and light assembly), registered-office address, authorized capital and registered share classes, number of directors, and registered-agent consent. The notary issues certified copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Apostilled or legalized power of attorney for non-resident subscribers
Passport copies of incorporators and first directors
Business plan or corporate object statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any drafting omission or typographical error in the deed is cured through a corrective public deed (escritura pública de rectificación). If the notary declines execution, the subscribers may instruct another notary of the same judicial district without commencing the process anew.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Inscription at the Public Registry (Mercantile Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Mercantil / Folio Electrónico.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarized incorporation deed together with the treasury fee payment receipt (papeleta del tesoro) at the Mercantile Section. The Registrar performs a legal-compliance review under Ley 32 de 1927, as amended. Upon admission, the company is assigned an electronic folio (Folio Electrónico), and a certificate of inscription is issued; the S.A. acquires separate legal personality only upon this inscription.
required_dossiers: Administrative authorization from the registered agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a formal or legal defect (reparo), counsel has 60 calendar days to file the corrective instrument. If the filing is rejected after the 60-day term, the fee may be restored and the deed resubmitted with all deficiencies remedied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Legalization of Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the S.A. and Registered Agent (Agente Residente); signatures may be notarized as required by the Company's bank or registry procedure.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board of directors meeting. The directors approve the First Board Resolution ratifying share subscription, adopting the registered office and statutory agent, appointing the President, Secretary and Treasurer, and authorizing bank account opening. Concurrently, legalize the corporate books (Share Register, Shareholders Minutes Book, Directors Minutes Book) at the Public Registry and update the officer appointments in the Folio Electrónico.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscription certificate
Original corporate books for stamping and sealing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If legalization of corporate books is rejected for binding, numbering or pagination defects, the books may be rebound and resubmitted with an explanatory request. Errors in officer registration are cured by filing an amending instrument with the Mercantile Section.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer ID (NIT) and Municipal Operating Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía del Municipio de Panamá or the district municipality where the warehouse is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the S.A. in the DGI taxpayer registry (Padrón) to obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and enroll in the electronic invoicing system (facturación electrónica). Within the statutory period after inscription, apply to the competent municipality for the Aviso de Operación / Certificado de Operación covering the kitting warehouse address and pay the municipal business tax applicable to ISIC 5210 / NAICS 493110 warehousing and fulfillment activities.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title deed for the warehouse
Identity document of the legal representative
Municipal operating permit application and zoning certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the tax registration, correct the document gaps and resubmit through the taxpayer portal. Municipal permit objections are cured by obtaining a valid use-of-soil certificate (certificado de uso de suelo) from the municipality and reapplying with the corrected zoning status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Health, Safety and Social Security Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) – Dirección de Salud y Seguridad Ocupacional.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the company as an employer with CSS to obtain the employer account number (cuenta patronal) and affiliate all warehouse workers to work-risk insurance. Submit the Occupational Health and Safety Program to MITRADEL and, where the workforce exceeds ten employees, constitute the Joint Occupational Health and Safety Committee. The program must address manual handling, packaging equipment guarding and emergency response for the kitting and assembly warehouse.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CSS enrollment is queried, resubmit corrected payroll forms and address proof. MITRADEL objections are cured by revising the safety program and presenting an amended compliance file with corrective action records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias; industrial registration is only a light-touch registry for warehousing and kitting, while the mandatory operational authorization is the municipal operating license issued by the local Alcaldía.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Certificado de Operación (Municipal Operating License) together with the Visto Bueno de Prevención de Incendios (Fire Safety Clearance).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (DEIA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Registro de Actividades de Bajo Riesgo Ambiental) – simplified environmental registration for logistics, warehousing and kitting operations under ISIC 5210 / NAICS 493110; no full EIA report is required unless hazardous-goods storage is added to the business scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal networks must comply with Resolución AG-058-2019 (pH 6.0-9.0; BOD5 ≤ 350 mg/L; TSS ≤ 350 mg/L; fats and oils ≤ 50 mg/L). Volatile organic compound emissions from adhesives and inks must remain below occupational permissible exposure limits through the use of water-based low-VOC materials. Solid waste, principally cardboard and plastic packaging, must be managed under the integrated waste regime of Ley 33 de 2018, with waste manifests maintained for any residual hazardous materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Visto Bueno de Prevención de Incendios) must be obtained from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá following on-site inspection of extinguishers, exits, emergency lighting and signage. Structural and seismic load clearance is evidenced by the municipal use-of-soil certificate and compliance with the Reglamento de Diseño Estructural (Law and F-200 building code provisions). Workplace clearance is granted by MITRADEL upon approval of the Occupational Health and Safety Program, including the accident registry, medical emergency plan and CSS work-risk contribution receipts.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign Sociedad Anónima must first register its constitutive deed and registered agent with the Registro Público de Panamá. With that proof, the legal representative files Form RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) before the DGI, either in person or through the Sede Electrónica, submitting corporate by-laws, appointment of resident agent, proof of registered address, and valid passport of directors. The DGI issues a provisional RUC immediately and a definitive RUC after verification. Accelerated issuance applies for companies solely engaging in export services or holding activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: Entity-level tax imposed only on Panamanian-source income; foreign-source income earned by the S.A. is outside Panama's income tax net. The entity is not eligible for pass-through treatment and is subject to annual corporate tax return plus the annual franchise tax (USD 300).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not offer a US-style check-the-box regime nor hybrid-mismatch elections. Statutory elections available include: (i) consolidated income tax filing for groups with ≥75% ownership upon DGI authorization; (ii) election to use the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime tax incentives for qualifying companies; (iii) simplified ITBMS regime for small taxpayers with annual turnover ≤ B/.36,000. No other hybrid or transparent entity elections are recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panamanian VAT/GST
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 (approximately USD 36,000) annual gross receipts triggers full mandatory ITBMS registration; however all businesses engaged in taxable supply chains (including foreign providers of digital services) are required to register for RUC/ITBMS regardless of turnover if no simplified regime is applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Factura Eléctronica is mandatory. Taxpayers must obtain DGI authorization and transmit e-invoices in XML via the DGI-web service API, incorporating a digital signature, QR code, and prior validation (CUF). Selected large taxpayers are subject to near-real-time digital clearance from DGI; no physical stamps are required. Foreign suppliers must issue e-invoices through an appointed legal representative's RUC.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods from Panama to a foreign destination are zero-rated for ITBMS purposes provided ownership passes abroad and goods physically leave Panama. Export-related services (logistics, warehousing, assembly, kitting, fulfilment) supplied to foreign recipients for use outside Panama also qualify for 0% rate. The taxpayer must retain a contractual export commitment, commercial invoice, customs exit declaration (DUA), and transport documentation. Sales to Panama's Colon Free Zone and other tax-exempt zones are treated as exports for ITBMS purposes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or letter from a Panamanian bank confirming foreign currency proceeds credited to the exporter's account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit teams cross-check export declarations, customs exit data, transport manifests, and bank statements. False zero-rating claims trigger retroactive assessment of the 7% ITBMS, surcharges (statutory interest), fines ranging from 50% to 100% of the omitted tax, and criminal tax fraud liability for the legal representative. DGI may also revoke RUC privileges and including the exporter in the public tax-delinquency registry.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as bank supervisory authority; Banco Nacional de Panamá as fiscal agent and designated government depositary; no central bank with monetary policy or foreign exchange administration exists because Panama is fully dollarized.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama has unrestricted de jure and de facto currency convertibility under a full dollarization regime where the U.S. dollar is legal tender. The capital account and current account are both freely convertible. There is no foreign-exchange licensing requirement, no central bank exchange-rate peg, and no permit for inward or outward remittance. Profit remittance may be executed through commercial banks without FX approval; the only practical constraints are corporate solvency, bank-source-of-funds rules, and applicable dividend withholding or territorial income tax compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no legal obligation to surrender export proceeds to any Panamanian authority. Panama does not impose mandatory conversion ratios, repatriation timeframes, or settlement requirements for export receipts. Export proceeds may be held in U.S. dollars domestically or retained abroad at the exporter discretion, subject only to banking record-keeping and AML/CFT obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with a strict licensing condition. Panama authorizes licensed electronic payment and electronic money issuers under SBP regulatory frameworks, and such regulated fintech institutions may offer cross-border collection and payout services. However, an unlicensed offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully maintain a Panamanian account or provide payment services to a Panama-incorporated operating company. A viable structure is to use an SBP-licensed EMI as a downstream payment conduit with the corporate operating account held at a tier-1 bank, or to use a licensed EMI that maintains a Panamanian banking custody relationship. A pure offshore EMI with no local license should not be used for treasury-critical disbursement rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and shareholder-control persons are generally not required to physically appear at a bank branch in every case if corporate documentation is notarized and apostilled, the full AML KYC file is completed, and a remote video interview is accepted by the bank. Most tier-1 Panamanian banks nevertheless require at least one initial in-person or videoconference interview with the beneficial owner, board resolution, and a duly empowered legal representative. The practical standard is to instruct local counsel to deliver the corporate dossier and act as introducer, after which remote signatories are acceptable for ongoing wire instructions using token-based or dual-control payment mechanisms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner not disclosed or shareholder register unavailable
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of the nominative shareholder register issued by the resident agent, initial share certificates, notarized UBO declaration forms, and a consolidated ownership-tree schedule identifying all individuals with greater than 10% ownership and all control positions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer share or bearer warrant risk in the Sociedad Anónima
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled written declaration that no bearer shares are outstanding, or evidence of immobilization/custody of bearer instruments with the resident agent, accompanied by a board resolution certifying the current shareholder register and the disenfranchisement of any unregistered bearer certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital injection from offshore shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from the remitting shareholder, evidence of prior corporate funds formation, audited financial records or shareholder-loan agreements, tax records from the shareholder jurisdiction, and a formal source-of-wealth letter countersigned by directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident management or fragmented KYC for directors who do not appear in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate resolution appointing a Panamanian legal representative or authorized signatory, certified copies of directors passports, professional reference from the introducing counsel, and a biometric or cryptographic identity verification report acceptable to the banks AML unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status or politically exposed person involvement in the distribution chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clear PEP declaration, source-of-funds documentation confirming independent commercial origin of capital, independent counsel opinion, and enhanced due-diligence file including family and business-relationship mapping where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial purpose mismatch between declared kitting/fulfillment operations and anticipated international receivables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer contracts, warehousing or fulfillment service agreements, purchase orders, ISIC 5210 scope narrative, vendor invoices, logistical documentation, and a treasury projection demonstrating the alignment of inbound capital, outbound trade payments, and the fulfillment activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed by SWIFT MT103 shareholder remittances from the originating bank to the Panamanian operating account. The bank will not require a foreign-exchange conversion because Panama uses USD, but the beneficiary bank will require the payment narrative to clearly state Equity Capital Contribution, Shareholder Loan, or Paid-in Surplus. The supporting file must include the shareholder board resolution, payment instruction, proof of corporate existence, and the banks source-of-funds form. Purpose-code fields are aligned to account-opening declarations rather than central-bank codes because Panama has no central-bank exchange-control reporting. Large or unusual injections may be held subject to compliance confirmation before posting to an available account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Eligible clearing rails for trade settlement include SWIFT MT103 customer transfers for direct supplier payments, MT101 for corporate-initiated batch transfers, MT202 for bank-to-bank interbank reimbursement, and commercial letters of credit issued by the Panamanian bank and advised through a foreign confirming bank. For domestic vendor disbursements the ACH Panama clearing system, RTP networks, and bank proprietary online-beneficiary systems can be used. U.S. dollar cross-border liquidity clears principally through the Panama bank correspondent relationships with U.S. Federal Reserve member banks and CHIPS or Fedwire. Commercial LC disbursements should include full transport, warehouse receipt, and inspection documents to match ISIC 5210 kitting activities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated treasury is naturally hedged because Panamanian bank accounts are operated in USD legal tender; no FX hedge is required for USD/USD flows.

Outright FX forwards contracted with Panamanian licensed banks or international counterparties for conversion between USD and third-country trade currencies are legally permissible without exchange-control approval.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with authorized international banks for currencies of trading partners where convertibility is restricted are permissible when executed under ISDA terms and treated as off-balance-sheet derivative exposures.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR, CNY, GBP, or other operating currencies are permissible as treasury risk-management instruments if documented under ISDA agreements and approved by the banks and securities licensing regime where applicable.

Interest-rate swaps and commodity-price hedging related to logistics and packaging input costs are permissible as non-speculative commercial hedging transactions, subject only to Panamanian bank risk-approval requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax payment ('Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas') with official proof of payment; USD 300 where authorized capital does not exceed USD 10,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, through the authorized bank or online payment portal; payment is matched to the corporation's registration with the Registro Público de Panamá.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 2 through June 15; the statutory deadline is June 15 of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 5% on the unpaid annual tax plus statutory interest; the registry will deny certificates of good standing; two or more consecutive unpaid years allow the Registro Público de Panamá to administratively strike off the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return ('Declaración Jurada de Renta') reporting Panama-source taxable income under the territorial system; a nil return is required if the corporation is registered with the RUC and has no taxable Panama-source activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 15 of the year following the December 31 fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines and monthly surcharges under the Código Fiscal, plus interest; continued non-filing risks suspension of the RUC, tax arrears certification, and exclusion from public and banking transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and corporate secretarial confirmation: verification of the Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book, share certificates, and registered office records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records maintained by the resident agent and the board of directors; no separate filing is submitted to the Registro Público unless demanded by law, court order, or tax audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within nine months after the fiscal year-end and, in practice, completed concurrently with the June 15 annual franchise tax payment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete registers create evidentiary prejudice in shareholder disputes, weaken corporate-veil protection, and may be penalized if the Registro Público or a court requires production of the records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updated beneficial ownership confirmation: written identification and verification of the natural persons who own 10% or more of the shares or otherwise exercise ultimate control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident agent (agente residente) maintaining the beneficial ownership record under Law 23 of 2015, Executive Decree 266 of 2017, and responsive to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the June 15 annual franchise tax deadline and within 15 days after any change in shareholding, allotment, or control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The resident agent must refuse or withdraw representation if beneficial ownership information is inaccurate or incomplete; statutory AML penalties may apply, and deficient records can prevent share transfers or issuance of good-standing certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit applies to an ordinary non-licensed Sociedad Anónima under Panama's General Corporation Law (Law 32 of 1927). An external statutory audit is triggered only where the corporation becomes a 'Gran Contribuyente' as segmented by the DGI, is a licensed bank, insurer, fiduciary, or securities issuer subject to SBP, SSP, or SMV supervision, or where shareholders holding at least 10% of issued shares lawfully demand a special audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Books may be maintained in United States dollars. Panama applies territorial taxation and generally accepts International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB, IFRS for SMEs, or generally recognized Panamanian accounting principles for non-regulated commercial entities. The resident agent must have access to the records if the DGI demands production.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama does not require a public annual UBO return. Under Law 23 of 2015, the resident agent must keep a current beneficial ownership register identifying every natural person holding 10% or more of share capital or exercising ultimate control. The company must provide a written annual confirmation and also report any transfer, allotment, or control change within 15 days; share transfers must be endorsed on the certificate and entered in the Register of Members. The resident agent may decline continued service if the annual confirmation is not provided.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per annum for a Panama law-firm resident agent and registered office service, excluding franchise tax and notarial fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,500 for a certified external audit if triggered; no audit cost is incurred where the exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama taxes territorial (Panamanian-source) income only. Opt-in consolidated small-taxpayer regime at 2% of gross revenue for entities up to B/. 200,000 gross income; NOL carryforward (5 years) and accelerated deductions; 'Export Services' regime (Law 41 of 2007) available for qualifying cross-border service providers (conditions apply).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 120 'Informe de Rentas' (annual corporate income tax return) filed on the DGI 'e-Tax 2.0' electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Panamanian-source and separately-identified foreign-source activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned S.A. must report all Panamanian-source operating revenue (warehousing, kitting, assembly); claim foreign-source exclusion only with documentary evidence of foreign activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs of goods sold, wages, rent, logistics and other operating expenses, evidenced by local invoices and payroll.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require valid receipts, banking trail and withholding compliance; related-party charges are limited to the arm's-length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after cost of sales and allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where income is predominantly Panama-source, no territorial apportionment is available; entire net profit is taxable at 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at 25% on the net taxable income, subject to the alternative minimum CAIR test.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident legal representative/authorized signatory must certify the return; DGI may require audited financial statements for gross revenues above B/. 3,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance credits, foreign tax credits (only for Panama-source recomputation), and the 4% provisional dividend tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advance payments are mandatory even for non-resident-owned entities; underpayments trigger the 25% rate plus surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Impuesto a Pagar / Crédito a Favor)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net tax payable (or refund) resulting from the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund is processed through the DGI's verification procedure and requires full filing compliance and registered bank account in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fines up to B/. 10,000; monthly surcharge of 5% on tax due (capped at 50%); interest of 1% per month; non-filing allows DGI estimated assessment and the loss of the company's good-standing status.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends distributed from profits subject to the 25% ISR; 5% from profits taxed under the small-taxpayer simplified (CAIR) regime; 15.5% on distributions from non-taxed profits; a 4% annual provisional dividend tax may be payable on retained profits and is creditable against the 10% WHT on later distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is limited (in force: Mexico, Spain, France, Portugal, South Korea, UAE and others). To claim relief, the foreign beneficial owner must deliver to the Panamanian payer: (i) a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the treaty state's tax authority, (ii) a Panama DGI treaty relief declaration confirming beneficial ownership and any LOB condition, and (iii) supporting shareholding evidence to obtain the treaty dividend rate (usually 5% for qualified shareholders, 10% as residual WHT).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to foreign non-resident beneficiaries is subject to a 6% statutory WHT; royalties and technical-service fees paid abroad are subject to a 12.5% statutory WHT; treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 5% and royalties to 10%; no WHT applies to payments for services objectively rendered entirely outside Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 250,000 (at par with USD) of related-party transactions in a fiscal year; beyond this threshold, the taxpayer must file the Form 351 related-party informative return and maintain a full transfer pricing study (Local File).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama applies an OECD-aligned economic substance doctrine: preferential regimes (Sem/SEF) were abolished (2010); a Panamanian S.A. claiming territorial exclusion or treaty benefits must prove real economic nexus (licensed premises, employees, local management, bank accounts, and books kept in Panama). An entity lacking local substance in the fulfillment/kitting business will be re-characterized as a pure invoice conduit, causing DGI assessment, denial of tax-residence certificates, and FATF/AML scrutiny.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating Panamanian-source kitting/fulfillment revenue as tax-exempt foreign-source income, maintaining false records, or omitting related-party transactions in the Form 120 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to 10 times the evaded tax plus surcharges, monthly interest, and criminal conviction: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; assets seized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers are individually liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax; conviction carries imprisonment, asset freezes, and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Panama S.A. as a pass-through invoicing vehicle with no employees, warehouse operations, or local management; nominee directors without control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization of income, retroactive denial of territorial exclusions/substance offsets, DGI penalties up to 100% of recomputed tax, cancellation of the company's tax-resident status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and shareholders may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and exposed to criminal charges for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party service fees, mark-ups, or intercompany loans priced above/below arm's length; absence of the required Form 351 or TP study once the B/. 250,000 threshold is pierced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjustment of taxable income, additional 25% ISR plus surcharge (up to 50%) and interest; penalties up to 100% of the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve the TP policy face personal fines and, where the adjustment arises from deliberate under-taxation, criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving large or unexplained ACH transfers from foreign counterparties without KYC and beneficial-owner disclosure; accepting cash; transacting with shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 AML penalties up to B/. 1,000,000; Law 70 of 2019 UBO Registry fines; money-laundering conviction carries imprisonment up to 12 years; freezing of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil and criminal responsibility attaches to directors, compliance officers, and legal representatives; travel bans and seizure of personal property are available remedies.
